title: The cull rail advertises 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' from a curve it already knows is stale; pressing it always refuses, and its advice ('re-integrate to refresh') reproduces the same stale curve
what_happened: The improvement curve is derived from the master that was just produced. Because that master contained only 1 registered frame (see the P0 above), the persisted curve has one point and a recommendation of {keepN: 1, predictedSnrGainPct: 0.0, reason: 'Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)'}. The cull rail then renders an enabled primary action 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' whose tooltip is 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best 1 subs (+0% SNR)'. Pressing it three times changed nothing (still 9 accepted in the DB) and toasted 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. So the control knows the curve does not match the 9 accepted subs, yet still renders a specific, quantified, actionable label -- and its remedy is to re-run the same integration that produced the stale curve.
expected: The rail must decide staleness at render time, not at press time. When the curve's population does not cover the currently-accepted subs, or when predictedSnrGainPct <= 0, show a disabled/absent action (or an explicit 'analysis out of date' chip) rather than a confident 'Keep best 1 (+0%)'. A control should not offer an operation it will unconditionally refuse.
repro: 1. Do the Integrate-now repro above (produces a 1-frame master). 2. A new button 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' appears beside Blink mode / Select-lasso. 3. Click it. 4. sqlite3 skotiq.db "select count(*) from captured_images where session_id=1 and is_accepted=1" -> still 9; toast reads 'Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-21.png, rsr-22.png, rsr-25.png show 'Keep best 1 (+0%)' while the header reads '9 accepted - 1 rejected'; AT-SPI tree after the click contains 'panel: Curve is out of date - re-integrate to refresh before culling'. DB improvement_curve_json for master 2: {"points":[{"n":1,...}],"recommendation":{"keepN":1,"keptIndices":[0],"predictedSnrGainPct":0.0,"reason":"Keep all 1 subs: already optimal (+0.0% SNR vs full stack)"},"population":[".../audit_L_001.fits"]} -- population length 1 vs 9 accepted, which is exactly the staleCurve guard in session_review_controller.dart:1377.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/widgets/sub_cull_rail.dart:473 (tooltip) and :475 (label 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct}%)'); guard in session_review_controller.dart:1354 cullToRecommended()
location_wrong: cullToRecommended() is at packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:1418-1480 in the rebuilt tree, not :1354 (the file grew 66 lines in the fix wave); sub_cull_rail.dart:473/475 are exact.
proposed_fix: Lift the population-vs-accepted comparison out of cullToRecommended() into a getter the rail reads while building, and gate the button on it plus predictedSnrGainPct > 0.
verdict_reasoning: The render-time/press-time asymmetry is exactly what the current source does, and the two cited widget lines are exact. sub_cull_rail.dart:274 passes the action through whenever `curve != null && curve.recommendation.keepN > 0` -- no population check, no gain check -- and :470-480 renders an enabled primary SkotiqButton labelled 'Keep best $keepN (+${gainPct.toStringAsFixed(0)}%)' (:475) inside a Tooltip 'Drop to the optimizer-recommended best $keepN subs (+…% SNR)' (:473). Every staleness test lives in the press handler instead: SessionReviewController.cullToRecommended() returns CullToRecommendedResult.staleCurve when the curve's population length differs from the accepted set, when paths duplicate, or when any population path is no longer accepted, and alreadyOptimal when keepN >= population.length. So in those states the control can only ever be pressed to be refused while still advertising a specific quantified action. This is NOT contingent on the P0 that produced the 1-frame master: any accept/reject after an integration diverges the population, and the alreadyOptimal case renders a '+0%' button that also refuses. Not re-driven live (needs a session with real FITS subs, which the scratch profile has none of); the source is unambiguous.

title: The 'Maximum Quality' integration profile is a placebo -- it produces byte-identical settings to Balanced
what_happened: Selecting each of the five integration profiles in turn and diffing the whole ADVANCED block of the accessibility tree: Fast changes the resampler to Bilinear, Few Subs changes rejection to Percentile clip with 0.2/0.1, Long Night / Gradient changes normalization Mode from Global to Local grid -- but Balanced and Maximum Quality produce an IDENTICAL 30-line block (`diff bal.txt maxq.txt` is empty) and an identical summary sentence. The source confirms it: IntegrationSettings.preset(maximumQuality) sets resampler=lanczos3, weighting=snrSquared, generateRejectionMap=true, cosmeticCorrection=true, outputBitDepth=f32 -- every one of which is already the constructor default that balanced inherits. The only field that differs between the two presets is sourcePreset, which is a label.
expected: A profile named 'Maximum Quality' must actually cost something in exchange for quality -- e.g. a tighter RANSAC threshold, more reference stars, local normalization, linear-fit/percentile rejection tuned for the sub count, or drizzle. As shipped, a user who deliberately picks Maximum Quality over Balanced for their best data gets exactly the same stack and is misled about it.
repro: 1. Session Review > Workbench > Integration settings > expand Advanced settings. 2. Click 'Balanced', capture the ALIGNMENT..DRIZZLE block of `drive_linux.py tree`. 3. Click 'Maximum Quality', capture again. 4. diff -> no differences. 5. Repeat for 'Long Night / Gradient' -> exactly one line differs (Global -> Local grid), proving the capture method detects real changes.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/maxq.txt -> identical (30 lines each); /tmp/ns-audit/bal.txt vs /tmp/ns-audit/ln.txt -> 1 line differs. Summary line unchanged: 'Will integrate 9 accepted subs using Winsorized sigma. Recommends culling the worst 10%.' for both. Source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/integration_settings.dart:737-745 vs the constructor defaults at :672,:676,:690,:691,:692.
proposed_fix: Give maximumQuality settings that actually differ (e.g. ransacThresholdPx 1.5, maxRefStars 120, normalization local, reject linearFit) -- or drop the chip. Also make the panel's one-line summary mention the knobs the chosen profile changed, so three profiles cannot render the same sentence.
verdict_reasoning: Read the current source. integration_settings.dart:737 is exactly `case IntegrationPreset.maximumQuality:` returning const IntegrationSettings(resampler: lanczos3, weighting: snrSquared, generateRejectionMap: true, cosmeticCorrection: true, outputBitDepth: f32, sourcePreset: maximumQuality). All five are already the constructor defaults (:670 lanczos3, :674 snrSquared, :688 true, :689 true, :690 f32), and balanced at :733 is `const IntegrationSettings(sourcePreset: balanced)` i.e. all defaults. The two objects therefore differ only in sourcePreset, and the only non-test consumer of sourcePreset anywhere in packages/ or apps/ is integration_settings_panel.dart:51 `active: _s.sourcePreset`, which decides which chip is highlighted. Nothing in toBridgeSettings or the native path reads it. Cited file:line exact.

title: Running an A/B recipe preview leaves a full 'Preview... 100%' progress bar pinned under the header forever, so the screen permanently claims a job is running
what_happened: Pressing 'Run both' in the A/B recipe compare panel puts a green progress strip labelled 'Preview... 100%' between the Narrative/Workbench toggle and the content. The two previews completed (the panel filled in with 'Frames kept tie 1 vs 1', 'Residual tie 0.00 vs 0.00 px', 'Integration time tie 00:05:00 vs 00:05:00'), but the strip was still on screen 13 minutes later, survived switching to Narrative and back, and is still present in the AT-SPI tree as 'panel: Preview...'.
expected: The strip must clear when the action that raised it finishes. The controller's own comment says a terminal 1.0 fraction 'is left on screen until the action's own completion handler clears it' -- integrate() does clear it (clearProgress/clearLiveProgress) but reIntegratePreview(), which is what the A/B panel calls, has no such handler, so the strip is orphaned.
repro: 1. Session Review > Workbench > A / B compare > 'Run both'. 2. Wait for both preview cards to fill in. 3. The strip under the header still reads 'Preview... 100%'. 4. Toggle to Narrative and back -- still there. 5. `drive_linux.py tree | grep Preview` still returns 'panel: Preview...'.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr-36.png (strip at 100% with the A/B results already rendered above it), rsr-37.png / rsr-38.png (same strip 13 min later, in Narrative and in Workbench). AT-SPI: 'panel: Preview...' persists across polls.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/session_review/session_review_controller.dart:515 _bindProgress() and :976 reIntegratePreview() (no clearProgress on completion); rendered by session_review_screen.dart:119 _ProgressStrip
location_wrong: Current lines: _bindProgress session_review_controller.dart:561 (not :515), reIntegratePreview :1022 (not :976), strip session_review_screen.dart:142-144 (not :119).
proposed_fix: Wrap reIntegratePreview (and the other seam-driven actions: runColorCalibration, runBackgroundExtraction, runDeconvolve, runStarReduction, runNarrowband) in the same try/finally that clears progress on exit, or clear progress centrally whenever `busy` transitions back to false.
verdict_reasoning: Traced the whole loop. native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/post_session.rs:838 ends the preview integrate with `emit_integration_progress("preview", FRACTION_DONE, None, None)` -- a terminal 1.0 on the shared stream. session_review_controller.dart:561-577 _bindProgress() writes every event onto state.progress and deliberately leaves a terminal fraction up ('left on screen until the action's own completion handler clears it'). session_review_screen.dart:142-144 renders _ProgressStrip for as long as progress != null, labelling the raw token as 'Preview…' (_phaseLabel :282). The only clears are integrate() (:796-797, :808-809) and the stream onError (:573). reIntegratePreview() at :1022-1042 -- what the A/B 'Run both' calls -- returns with no clear on any path, so the 100% strip is orphaned. Not re-driven live (needs FITS subs on disk).

title: A single sub that fails alignment aborts the entire Stack & Share run and deletes the partial result, even though the code counts 'rejected' frames as a normal outcome
what_happened: With 'Apply calibration' off the stacker initialised on audit_L_024.fits with 34 stars, then the very first follower frame (audit_L_018.fits) was rejected for alignment residual and the whole run died: the dialog showed 'Stack & Share failed', no stacked_results row was written, and the log shows 'Live stacker stopped and resources released' one millisecond after the rejection -- frames 019-024 were never attempted. The native layer treats this as a per-frame rejection (it increments stats.rejected_alignment_failures and returns Err), and the Dart loop even has a framesRejected counter for exactly this case, but the counter is dead code: _addStackFrame is awaited without a try/catch, so the Err becomes an exception that escapes the for-loop into the run-level catch, which deletes the incomplete stacked_results row and rethrows.
expected: A frame that fails to register must be counted and skipped, and the run must continue with the remaining subs -- exactly what the framesRejected counter was written for. Losing an entire night's stack to one satellite-trailed or wind-shaken sub is the single most expensive failure mode this feature has. The dialog should end with 'Stacked 6 of 8 subs - 2 rejected (alignment)'.
repro: 1. Imaging > Stack > Stack & Share on an 8-sub session, turn 'Apply calibration' off, press Start. 2. Watch the log: 'Adding frame to stack: .../audit_L_018.fits' then 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' then 'Live stacker stopped'. 3. Dialog reads 'Stack & Share failed'. 4. sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select count(*) from stacked_results' -> unchanged (1, the pre-seeded row); no new row for this run.
evidence: App log 2026-08-02T14:53:10: 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_018.fits' / 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' / 'Live stacker stopped and resources released'. UI: 'Stack & Share failed - SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Alignment residual too high: 10.34px (max 10.00px))'. DB: stacked_results count 1 before and after.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_and_share_service.dart:328 (`final result = await _addStackFrame(...)` inside the followers loop, no try/catch) and the now-unreachable framesRejected accounting at :335-340; run-level catch that deletes the row at :484.
proposed_fix: Wrap the _addStackFrame await in a try/catch that increments framesRejected, records the reason, emits progress and continues; only fail the run if the surviving stacked count is below a floor (e.g. < 2 frames). Surface the rejected count and the most common reason in the completion state.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live, twice. With 'Apply calibration' off: 'Live stacker initialized: 512x512 reference with 34 stars' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_017.fits' / 'Frame 2 stacked (2 total, 0 rejected)' / 'Adding frame to stack: audit_L_018.fits' / 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' / 'Live stacker stopped and resources released' 1 ms later. Frames 019-024 never attempted; dialog read 'Stack & Share failed - SkotiqError.imageError(field0: Alignment residual too high: 10.34px (max 10.00px))'; stacked_results unchanged at 3 rows before and after both runs. Cited lines are exact: stack_and_share_service.dart:328 is literally 'final result = await _addStackFrame(' inside 'for (final frame in followers)' with no try/catch, and :335-340 is the framesRejected accounting. That counter is genuinely unreachable: every rejection path in stacking.rs (too few stars :447, too few matches :471, residual too high :495) returns Err, and the only Ok path accumulates and increments the stacked count. Location nit: the finding cites :484 for the run-level catch that deletes the row; in the current file the catch is at :486 and the deleteResult call at :493.

title: Registration reports a 10.34px alignment residual for a pure 2.2px translation of the same 40-star field, so even the working path cannot stack; match_radius_px defaults to 50px
what_happened: audit_L_018.fits and audit_L_024.fits contain the SAME 40 stars offset by a rigid ~2.2px translation -- every star in 024 has a counterpart in 018 at distance 2.0-3.16px (median 2.24px), verified independently with a peak-finder and a nearest-neighbour match. The stacker matched 28 pairs and then computed an alignment residual of 10.34px, which exceeded its own 10.00px ceiling, so the frame was rejected. A correct affine fit on that geometry gives a sub-pixel residual. With match_radius_px defaulting to 50.0 and match_flux_tolerance to 0.7 in a 512x512 frame whose mean star separation is ~81px, the matcher is free to pair a star with a neighbour 50px away, and a handful of such wrong pairs is enough to wreck the least-squares fit and inflate the residual.
expected: Registering two frames that differ by a 2.2px shift must produce a residual well under 1px and the frame must be accepted. Separately, max_alignment_residual_px = 10.0 is not a meaningful quality gate -- a 10px misalignment folded into the stack is a visibly smeared image; NINA/DSS-class tolerances are a fraction of a pixel.
repro: 1. Stack & Share on the 8-sub session with 'Apply calibration' off. 2. Log: 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)'. 3. Independently measure the true offset: peak-find both FITS (40 peaks each) and nearest-neighbour match -> min 2.00px, median 2.24px, max 3.16px.
evidence: App log 'WARN Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)'. Measured geometry: n024=40, n018=40, match distances min 2.0 / median 2.24 / max 3.16 px. Config defaults at native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs:85-104.
where: native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stacking.rs:91 match_radius_px: 50.0, :92 match_flux_tolerance: 0.7, :94 max_alignment_residual_px: 10.0; residual computed at :487 compute_alignment_residual and the fit at :485 compute_affine_transform.
proposed_fix: Scale match_radius_px to the frame (e.g. a small multiple of the measured FWHM, or an iterative coarse-then-fine match seeded by a translation estimate) rather than a fixed 50px, and reject pairs whose residual is an outlier before the final fit (RANSAC / sigma-clipped refit). Then tighten max_alignment_residual_px to ~1px so the gate means something.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live and deterministically: two consecutive Stack & Share runs on the same 8 subs both logged 'Frame rejected: alignment residual 10.34px exceeds max 10.00px (28 matches)' for audit_L_018.fits against reference audit_L_024.fits, to the same 0.01 px. I measured the true geometry independently with my own FITS reader + peak finder + nearest-neighbour match (no app code): both frames contain 40 stars, every star pairs at 2.21-2.25 px, offset is a pure translation dx = -1.001, dy = +1.999 with per-star scatter 0.008/0.006 px — a rigid fit on correct pairs gives an essentially zero residual, so 10.34 px is ~5× wrong, not marginal. Config defaults cited are exact (stacking.rs:91 match_radius_px 50.0, :92 match_flux_tolerance 0.7, :94 max_alignment_residual_px 10.0) as are the fit/residual sites (:485, :487). CAVEATS: (a) I verified the transform math is self-consistent — compute_affine_transform is a standard Procrustes rigid fit and AffineTransform::apply at :272-276 applies exactly that transform — so the inflated residual cannot come from a fit/apply mismatch; that supports but does not prove the finding's 50 px-radius story. (b) 'even the working path cannot stack' is too strong: audit_L_017.fits (offset dx -2.0, dy -1.0) aligned and stacked fine in the same run, so the failure is per-frame. (c) An alternative cause to exclude before touching match_radius_px: bad CENTROIDS out of detect_stars would produce the identical observable, and the same detector returns 0 stars on audit_L_001.fits which my peak finder reads as 40 clean stars. (d) The real fix is likely a robust fit (RANSAC / iterative outlier rejection); tightening the radius alone would relocate the defect. Note the post-session integration path (registration.rs) reports 0.11 px on comparable frames, so this is specific to the live-stacker registration.

title: The Share Card's metadata strip is clipped: it renders 'M51  Integration 00:35:00  Frames 7  Fil…' and the filter is cut off the right edge
what_happened: Stack result > Share Card exports a 512x512 RGB PNG whose bottom caption bar reads 'M51   Integration  00:35:00   Frames  7   Fil' and then hits the right edge mid-word. The caption is laid out at a font size derived from the image HEIGHT (ShareCardSpec.fontScale defaults to ShareCardFontScale.scaleToHeight) with no measurement against the available WIDTH, so any card narrower than the caption needs simply truncates. This is the artefact the feature exists to produce -- the thing a user posts publicly -- and it ships with the text running off the edge.
expected: Either measure the caption and shrink the font / wrap to a second line until it fits the card width, or render the card on a fixed-size canvas (e.g. 1200x1200 or 1200x675) with the image letterboxed, so the caption geometry is independent of the stack's pixel dimensions.
repro: 1. Produce any stack result whose image is 512px wide. 2. Stack result screen > 'Share Card' > save to a .png. 3. Open the PNG and read the bottom strip.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/rsr-sharecard.png (copied to /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-12.png): 512x512, bit depth 8, colour type 2; bottom bar reads 'M51 | Integration 00:35:00 | Frames 7 | Fil'. The result screen and the AstroBin sidecar both carry 'Filter L', so the data is present -- only the rendering truncates.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/stack_and_share_models.dart:644-676 ShareCardSpec (layout bottomBar, fontScale scaleToHeight); composition in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/stack_share_export_service.dart
location_wrong: The truncating code is packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/share_card_renderer.dart:360-447 (_drawBottomBar), not stack_share_export_service.dart (which only forwards at :344); the spec itself is stack_and_share_models.dart:642-676 as cited.
proposed_fix: Add a width-fitting pass: measure the composed caption at the height-derived size and reduce the size (or split into two rows) until it fits within the card width minus padding. Add a regression test that renders a 512-wide card and asserts the caption's measured width is <= card width.
verdict_reasoning: Recomputed the geometry myself rather than trusting the screenshot. I ran the shipped ShareCardRenderer against the exact spec stack_result_screen.dart:852 builds (title 'M51', stats Integration 00:35:00 / Frames 7 / Filter L, targetWidth=targetHeight=result dimensions=512). fontForHeight(512) -> 20.5 -> img.arial24, lineHeight 28, pad 14, gap 11. Summing xAdvance exactly as _drawBottomBar does: 'M51' 14..60, 'Integration  00:35:00' 93..311, 'Frames  7' 344..452, 'Filter  L' starts at 485 and needs 80px -> ends at 565, i.e. 53px past the 512px right edge. Rendering the PNG for real and scanning the caption band shows bright glyph pixels running to column 511, so the last segment is cut mid-word as reported. Nothing measures the caption against the card WIDTH -- the only width logic is `if (x >= bitmap.width - pad) break;` and drawString clips the remainder.

title: First Light's 'Could not load candidates' Retry button does not re-query -- the error survives Retry and a tab round-trip, and only a full app restart clears it
what_happened: The First Light candidate list threw while decoding one row and rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-042' with a Retry button. I then fixed the offending value in the database (tile_id 'tile-042' -> 261982, confirmed typeof=integer) and pressed Retry twice, and switched to the Science sub-tab and back: the identical error text -- including the stale 'tile-042' fragment -- was still on screen. Only killing and restarting the app made the list load. The same staleness affects the success path: after the list HAS loaded, editing a detection's row (kind) outside the app and switching sub-tabs away and back still rendered the old value, so the candidate list is fetched once per app launch and is never refetched.
expected: Retry must invalidate the provider and re-run the query -- that is the entire contract of a Retry button. And the candidate list must refresh as new detections arrive: the panel's own header promises 'Every solved frame is differenced against your deep sky atlas ... Anything that appeared, moved, or brightened on a deep patch lands here to review', which is false if the list is a one-shot read taken at app launch.
repro: 1. Put a row in transient_detections whose tile_id is not parseable (SQLite type affinity permits a TEXT value in the INTEGER column). 2. Analytics > Science > First Light -> 'Could not load candidates'. 3. Fix the row: update transient_detections set tile_id=261982. 4. Press Retry -> same error. 5. Switch to Science and back to First Light -> same error. 6. Restart the app -> the candidate renders correctly.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-15.png (error state with Retry). AT-SPI tree after two Retry presses and a tab round-trip still contains 'panel: Could not load candidates' / 'FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) tile-042'. DB at that moment: select id,tile_id,typeof(tile_id) -> 1|261982|integer. After a restart the same tab shows 'Possible unknown transient / 13h 29m 52.7s +47 11 43.1'.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/first_light/first_light_view.dart (candidate list provider + the Retry action on its error state)
location_wrong: The Retry action is NOT missing an invalidate. first_light_view.dart:406-410 already reads onPressed: () => ref.invalidate(firstLightCandidatesProvider). The provider being invalidated lives in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_detections_provider.dart:138-152 — a StreamProvider returning transientDetectionsDaoProvider.watchRecentDetections(...), i.e. a cached Drift query stream. A fixer sent to first_light_view.dart will find a correct-looking Retry and may wrongly close this as a false positive; the broken link is that invalidating the provider does not produce a fresh execution of the underlying Drift stream.
proposed_fix: Make Retry call ref.invalidate on the candidates provider (and make the provider watch the detections table as a stream, so new candidates appear during a run instead of at next launch). Separately, decode a row defensively so one unparseable row is skipped and reported rather than failing the whole list.
verdict_reasoning: Symptom reproduced step for step. I set transient_detections.tile_id to the TEXT value 'tile-042' (SQLite affinity allows it), restarted, and Analytics > Science > First Light rendered 'Could not load candidates / FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1) / tile-042' with a Retry button. I fixed the row from outside the app (tile_id=261982, typeof integer), pressed Retry twice, and switched to the Science sub-tab and back: identical error text including the stale 'tile-042' fragment every time. Killing and restarting made the same tab render 'Possible unknown transient / 13h 29m 52.7s +47° 11' 43.1"'. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) see location_wrong — Retry does call ref.invalidate, so the defect is downstream of it. (2) The finding's second claim — that an external row edit not appearing after a tab switch proves 'the candidate list is fetched once per app launch and is never refetched' — does not follow and I am NOT confirming it: the provider is a Drift watch stream, and Drift's stream store cannot observe writes made by a different process on the same file, so an unnoticed external sqlite3 edit says nothing about whether in-app detections push through. That sub-claim needs a re-test with an in-app write. Severity: the dead Retry is real, but the only demonstrated route into the error state is a value the app itself never writes, so P2 fits better than P1.

title: In the Submit-discovery dialog all three network chips are dead on a default install, and only the currently-selected network's blocker is explained
what_happened: Submit discovery opens with Network = TNS and an amber line 'TNS submission needs your bot id/name, reporting group, data source, reporter, and api key -- configure them in Settings > Science.' Clicking the AAVSO chip does nothing (verified twice, once with coordinates measured from a cropped region shot so the hit point was unambiguous); TNS stays selected. Preview and 'Submit to TNS' are equally inert -- no dialog, no snackbar, no log line, no file. All three chips are disabled because _formatEnabled is false for each: AAVSO needs an observer code AND a magnitude zero point, MPC needs an observatory code AND a mover-class detection, TNS needs the five bot fields. None of the chips render a disabled affordance, and the panel prints a reason only for the format that happens to be selected, so a user who wants the AAVSO export -- the cheapest one to enable, it needs a single settings field -- gets a chip that silently ignores them and a message about TNS credentials that has nothing to do with their problem.
expected: A disabled chip must look disabled and must say why on hover/press. Better: list all three networks with their individual status ('AAVSO - needs observer code', 'MPC - not a moving object', 'TNS - needs bot key') so the user can see at a glance which one is reachable and what it costs.
repro: 1. Seed a confirmed newSource detection. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light > Submit. 3. Click AAVSO -> nothing; TNS stays selected (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-19.png vs rsr2-20.png are identical). 4. Click Preview -> nothing, no snackbar within 1s, nothing in the log.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-18.png (whole dialog), rsr2-19.png and rsr2-20.png (network row before and after an AAVSO click, byte-for-byte the same state). Source: transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 (`onTap: enabled ? ... : null`) and :142-148 (the reason block only renders _disabledReason for `_format`).
proposed_fix: Render disabled chips at reduced opacity with a tooltip carrying that format's own _disabledReason, and show a per-format status list instead of a single reason line.
verdict_reasoning: Verified in source at the cited lines and reproduced live. transient_report_panel.dart:127-140 renders the three chips with `onTap: enabled ? ... : null`, and :142-151 renders _disabledReason ONLY for the selected `_format`. _formatEnabled at :343-367 gates every format on d.reviewed, then aavso on aavsoAvailable + non-empty settings.aavsoObserverCode, mpc on a non-empty mpcObservatoryCode + a plausible-mover kind, tns on complete bot creds -- all false on a default install. skotiq_chip.dart:65-68 returns the bare chip when onTap is null: same fill, border and text colour as an enabled unselected chip, no Semantics, no cursor change, so a disabled chip is indistinguishable and silently swallows the tap. Preview/Copy at :296-320 are gated the same way. title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude, so a self-discovered transient is announced as 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE'
what_happened: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders the First Light detection as 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed - possible new transient / 13h 29m 52s +47 11' 43" / mag 2.4 [NAKED EYE]'. The detection row has delta_mag = -2.35 (a brightness CHANGE in magnitudes relative to the atlas template) and no photometric zero point anywhere in the pipeline -- there is no apparent magnitude for this object at all. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 sets `magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs()`, and the card at transient_card.dart:581 then buckets `magnitude <= 6.0` as NAKED EYE, <= 10 BINOCULAR, <= 14 SMALL SCOPE. Because a difference-image delta magnitude of more than ~6 is essentially impossible, EVERY First Light self-discovery that has a measured delta is announced as a naked-eye or binocular object. The app is telling the user they have found a magnitude-2.4 supernova -- brighter than Polaris, and the brightest supernova in recorded history.
expected: Do not populate the alert's apparent-magnitude field from a delta magnitude. Either leave magnitude null (the card already handles a null magnitude by omitting the chip) and show the delta separately as 'Δ2.35 mag', or compute a real apparent magnitude from a photometric zero point when one exists. The NAKED EYE / BINOCULAR / SMALL SCOPE bucketing must never run on a delta.
repro: 1. Insert a transient_detections row with kind='newSource', delta_mag=-2.35, snr=18.4, reviewed=1. 2. Restart the app. 3. Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts. 4. Read the chip on the alert card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-21.png: green chip 'mag 2.4  NAKED EYE' next to a card titled 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova'. DB: select id,kind,delta_mag,snr,fwhm from transient_detections -> 1|newSource|-2.35|18.4|2.41. There is no apparent-magnitude column on the table at all and photometric_transforms is empty, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction.
proposed_fix: Add a distinct deltaMag field to TransientAlert and leave `magnitude` null for First Light detections; render 'Δ 2.35 mag brighter' instead of 'mag 2.4', and suppress the brightness bucket entirely when only a delta is known.
verdict_reasoning: Code, data and UI all check out. transient_alert_mapper.dart:20 is exactly 'final magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs();' and is passed straight into TransientAlert.magnitude, the apparent-magnitude field every alert surface consumes. transient_card.dart:580-588 _getBrightnessInfo buckets magnitude<=6 NAKED EYE / <=10 BINOCULAR / <=14 SMALL SCOPE, called at :532 and rendered as 'mag ${magnitude.toStringAsFixed(1)}' at :553. DB: transient_detections has exactly one row, kind=newSource delta_mag=-2.35 snr=18.4, and the table has no apparent-magnitude column at all, so 2.4 cannot be an apparent magnitude by construction. Confirmed live on my own profile: Analytics > Science > Observing Alerts renders 'NS J13.50+47.2 / Supernova - Unconfirmed — possible new transient / mag 2.4 / NAKED EYE'. Because a difference-image delta larger than ~6 mag is essentially impossible, every First Light self-discovery with a measured delta is bucketed NAKED EYE or BINOCULAR. Cited file:line is precise.

title: Confirming a First Light candidate does not update the Observing Alerts tab beside it: the same detection reads 'Confirmed' on one sub-tab and 'New' on the next
what_happened: On Analytics > Science > First Light I pressed Confirm on the candidate; the card's badge changed to 'Confirmed', the toast read 'Marked as confirmed.' and the database row updated (reviewed=1). Switching one tab across to Observing Alerts -- the same screen, the same detection, mapped through transientAlertFromDetection -- the card still carries a blue 'New' badge and sits under the 'New' filter. transientAlertFromDetection maps reviewed -> TransientAlertState.acknowledged, so the alert list is being served from a snapshot taken at app launch and is not rebuilt when the detection changes.
expected: Two views of one row, on two tabs of one screen, must not disagree. Confirming in First Light should immediately move the alert out of 'New'.
repro: 1. Seed a confirmed-able detection and restart the app. 2. Analytics > Science > First Light > Confirm (badge becomes 'Confirmed', toast 'Marked as confirmed.'). 3. sqlite3 -> reviewed=1. 4. Click 'Observing Alerts'. 5. The card shows the 'New' badge.
evidence: AT-SPI at 11:10 on First Light: 'Confirmed' twice plus 'panel: Marked as confirmed.'; DB at that instant: 1|newSource|1|0 (reviewed=1). /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rsr2-21.png at 11:14 on Observing Alerts: 'New' badge on the same detection. Mapping that should have produced 'acknowledged': packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper.dart:41-46.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/transient_alert_provider.dart (the alert list is not invalidated when transient_detections changes)
location_wrong: Cause is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/transients/transients_screen.dart:122/143/167-172 + widgets/transient_card.dart:56 (card state comes from transientAlertStatesProvider; TransientAlert.state is ignored), NOT 'transient_alert_provider.dart -- the alert list is not invalidated'; the list IS re-merged via ref.listen at transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556.
proposed_fix: Have the alert provider watch the detections table (or invalidate it from the confirm/dismiss mutation) so both sub-tabs read one source of truth.
verdict_reasoning: Symptom REPRODUCED LIVE on the rebuilt bundle: seeded detection id 1 (newSource, reviewed=0), Analytics > Science > First Light > Confirm -> DB reviewed=1 and the card badge reads 'Confirmed' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-12.png); one tab across, Observing Alerts shows the same detection ('NS J13.50+47.2', Supernova) with a blue 'New' badge (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sr-11.png). But the finding's cause and 'where' are wrong, which matters because the cited file is not the one to fix. transient_alert_mapper.dart:66-70 does map reviewed -> acknowledged, and the list IS rebuilt: activeTransientAlertsProvider is a StreamProvider.autoDispose holding `ref.listen(allTransientDetectionsProvider, ...)` (transient_alert_provider.dart:552-556), and allTransientDetectionsProvider is a drift watchRecentDetections live query (transient_detections_provider.dart:95-100) that re-emits on the local markReviewed write. The badge stays 'New' because the Observing Alerts UI never reads the alert's own state: transients_screen.dart:122 watches transientAlertStatesProvider, :143 does `states[alert.id]`, and transient_card.dart:56 falls back to newAlert when that map has no entry; _filterAlerts :167-172 puts exactly those under 'New'. That map is only ever populated from persisted `transient_alert_state_<id>` settings rows written by the user's own queue/dismiss actions (:683-810) -- nothing seeds it from TransientAlert.state, so the mapper's `acknowledged` is dead on this surface.
